findings.reason: The original formula renders correctly, but a concrete explanatory diagram is warranted under the expanded editorial scope: it makes the two separate operations visible, first splitting by K-orbits on G/H and then identifying each support summand using its stabilizer. The complete proof does not remove this explanatory benefit. Both authentic original PNGs were viewed separately at original resolution; the second is a blank continuation.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section defining U_s and J_s, explaining the orbit-stabilizer bijection, and giving the two-stage K-module decomposition in a fenced TikZ figure.

correction: Added only final Remarks with the existing support decomposition and direct sum of the explicitly constructed Theta_s maps; no claim of additional naturality or commutative square.

diagram_math_checks.objects: G finite; H,K subgroups; S represents K\G/H; U_s=K intersect sHs^{-1}.
diagram_math_checks.check: The K-orbit of the left coset sH is KsH/H. Its stabilizer consists of k in K with ksH=sH, equivalently s^{-1}ks in H, hence exactly U_s. The map K/U_s -> KsH/H, kU_s -> ksH, is well defined, injective and surjective, and respects the left K-action.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local double-coset definition and proof step 1.1; no change to the chosen representatives.

diagram_math_checks.objects: I=Ind_H^G W, I_s the subspace supported on KsH. First arrow Res_K^G I -> direct sum over S of I_s.
diagram_math_checks.check: Each KsH is right H-stable, so cutting a covariant function to that support preserves covariance. It is left K-stable, so this projection commutes with the action (x.f)(g)=f(x^{-1}g). The partition of G gives an inverse by summing components. Thus the displayed left-to-right arrow is a K-module isomorphism.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof step 1.1 and the local covariant-function definition of induction.

diagram_math_checks.objects: {}^sW is a representation of sHs^{-1}; restrict to U_s, then induce to K to obtain J_s. Theta_s:I_s -> J_s.
diagram_math_checks.check: The restriction has domain U_s <= sHs^{-1}, and induction has target K because U_s <= K. For u=shs^{-1} in U_s, Theta_s(f)(ku)=f(ksh)=h^{-1}f(ks)=u^{-1}Theta_s(f)(k), with conjugate action u.w=h.w. Thus Theta_s(f)(k)=f(ks) has exactly the target covariance convention.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Conjugate-representation definition; proof step 2.1; induced covariant-function definition.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Second arrow direct sum I_s -> direct sum J_s labelled direct sum Theta_s.
diagram_math_checks.check: The inverse on the s component is f_phi(ksh)=h^{-1}phi(k), extended by zero. If ksh=k′sh′, then k^{-1}k′=sh(h′)^{-1}s^{-1} in U_s, and the J_s covariance gives identical values. For x in K, Theta_s(x.f)(k)=f(x^{-1}ks)=(x.Theta_s(f))(k), so the map is K-equivariant. This verifies the displayed direction and isomorphism label.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Characters of the composite K-module isomorphism.
diagram_math_checks.check: Taking characters converts the finite direct sum into the sum stated in the theorem with the same S, U_s, restriction domain sHs^{-1}, and induction codomain K. The diagram asserts only the two existing module isomorphisms; it adds no natural-isomorphism or commutativity claim.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof step 5.1 and F1. The original rigorous proof remains byte-for-byte intact and independent of the illustration.
